open_points.subject: Port declarations in contracts, bindings and flows
open_points.text: M01 gives every Port a `direction`, while M03, M11 and M13 also place ports in separate `inputs` and `outputs` collections; A02 checks names and classes but never says what happens when a port's `direction` disagrees with the collection containing it.
open_points.question: Must a port's `direction` match its enclosing input/output collection, and which check refuses a mismatch?
options: Refuse the owner at authoring or composition
Ignore `direction` and infer it from the collection
Ignore the collection and use the port's `direction`
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the request before issuing or keeping the owner.

open_points.subject: File-port value schemas
open_points.text: M01 says every port has a `value_schema`, including file ports, but A03 validates a file output only as `bytes`, A09 validates it by media type and spool limits, and K-10 says the kernel does not inspect file content.
open_points.question: What does a file port's `value_schema` describe, and when, if ever, is a file or file fixture validated against it?
options: Treat it only as an exact edge-compatibility label
Validate file metadata against it
Restrict file ports to one prescribed schema form
open_points.default_guess: Treat the schema as an exact compatibility label and validate file bytes only by type, media type and size.

open_points.subject: Guard ports
open_points.text: A05 rule 1 phase 4 requires a guard port to be a `one` output with a closed-set schema, but does not require `value` carriage; A13 rule 4 then compares the guard port's value with the guard value.
open_points.question: Can a file output be used as a guard port, and if so how is a file compared with a JSON guard value?
options: Require guard ports to have `value` carriage
Permit file guards and compare file bytes
Permit file guards and compare file digests
open_points.default_guess: Require `value` carriage and fail the proof for a file guard port.

open_points.subject: Guard-value equality
open_points.text: A13 says a guarded edge delivers when the guard port's value `equals its guard value`, without defining equality for JSON numbers, objects or arrays.
open_points.question: Which equality relation decides a guard: canonical-JSON byte equality, JSON Schema enum equality, or host-language equality?
options: Canonical JCS bytes are equal
JSON Schema equality is used
Python equality is used
open_points.default_guess: Compare canonical JCS bytes.

open_points.subject: Authored trial-case shape
open_points.text: A04 rule 1 says inputs and expected outputs must `fit` the contract's ports and mentions checking presence, but never states whether the input map must contain exactly every input port or whether a present `expected_outputs` map must contain exactly every output port.
open_points.question: Are missing and extra trial inputs refused, and when expected outputs are present must they cover exactly all output ports or may they be partial?
options: Inputs and expected outputs must each be exact maps
Inputs are exact but expected outputs may be partial
Both maps may be partial
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and, when present, exact expected outputs.

open_points.subject: Sandbox determinism
open_points.text: A03 requires only the listed clock and randomness traps and fixed `PYTHONHASHSEED`, while required test 6 says `The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.` Standard Python still exposes nondeterministic observations such as object identities, process scheduling and concurrent-process behavior.
open_points.question: What additional restriction or qualification makes deterministic execution and deterministic admission enforceable?
options: Ban or trap every remaining nondeterministic observation
Define determinism only for conforming implementations and detect mismatches through trials
Remove the guarantee that repeated executions have equal output
open_points.default_guess: Treat deterministic output as an obligation of conforming code and classify use of a closed, explicitly enumerated set of nondeterministic facilities as a sandbox violation.

open_points.subject: Sandbox exchange directory and runner protocol
open_points.text: A03 grants the environment `one private exchange directory` and says `run` receives Python values and bytes, but does not define the directory layout, serialization protocol, file names, file permissions, inherited descriptors, or which parts are accessible to implementation code.
open_points.question: How are inputs, outputs and trap reports transferred across the sandbox boundary, and what may untrusted code observe or modify in the exchange directory?
options: A fixed documented file protocol
Private parent-runner IPC with no protocol files visible to user code
Implementation-defined runner files
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed runner-owned protocol and expose no control or result files to the implementation beyond its `run` argument.

open_points.subject: Sandbox process bound
open_points.text: A03 says `process_count` is enforced with `setrlimit (address space, processes)` but does not say whether the runner counts toward the limit, whether threads count, or how the limit is isolated from other executions by user identity.
open_points.question: Exactly which processes or threads count against `process_count`, and is the requested bound for user-created children or for the whole sandbox environment?
options: Count the runner and every descendant process
Count only descendants created by implementation code
Count processes and threads together
open_points.default_guess: Count the runner and all descendants as processes in a sandbox-private user namespace; threads do not consume process slots unless the operating-system limit does so.

open_points.subject: Admission verdicts across kernel releases
open_points.text: A04 reuses any AdmissionVerdict for the same implementation and corpus digest, while A20 permits a new release to change the Python runtime and dependencies. Neither TrialExecution nor AdmissionVerdict identifies the release or sandbox runtime that produced it.
open_points.question: Does an admission verdict from an earlier release remain valid after runtime or dependency changes, or must the release/runtime identity participate in verdict validity?
options: Old verdicts remain valid forever
A new release requires fresh admission
Only releases declaring sandbox compatibility may reuse verdicts
open_points.default_guess: Require fresh admission when the sandbox runtime or dependency identity changes.

open_points.subject: Runs across kernel releases
open_points.text: A12 says a run pins the flow version and function implementations, but not the kernel release or sandbox runtime; A14 may re-execute a function after restart, and A20 allows a new release to change dependencies and ceilings.
open_points.question: After upgrading and restarting, under which runtime and ceiling set does an unfinished run continue, and can a re-executed pure function use a different runtime from its earlier attempts?
options: Pin the originating release semantics to the run
Continue under the newly installed release
Refuse recovery of runs created by an incompatible release
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to advance an unfinished run under an incompatible runtime and require release compatibility to be explicit.

open_points.subject: Mapped-list size failure across releases
open_points.text: A13 derives a mapped node's failure from its element records and the current `stored_value_bytes_max`, with no aggregate failure record; A20 says a new release may change ceilings and that recorded executions are never reinterpreted.
open_points.question: Which release's `stored_value_bytes_max` is used to derive an unfinished or historical mapped node's aggregate result after an upgrade?
options: The ceiling in force when the run started
The ceiling in force when the list is first delivered
The current release ceiling whenever the trace is read
open_points.default_guess: Use and persist the ceiling in force when the run started.

open_points.subject: Draft-write authority
open_points.text: M26 requires a draft-write EffectAttempt to name `the flow activation under which the run started`, but M19 and A12 pin only `flow_version_id` and function implementations, not the FlowActivation record. The same version can be activated again at a different store position.
open_points.question: How does a run durably identify the exact FlowActivation that authorizes its draft-write sends, including after restart?
options: Store the FlowActivation position on the Run
Derive the latest preceding activation from store order
Use only the flow-version identity
open_points.default_guess: Store the exact FlowActivation identity on the Run at creation.

open_points.subject: Startup recovery of multiple runs
open_points.text: A14 rule 5 says the kernel derives unfinished runs `oldest first in store order` and advances every run left `running`, but does not say whether all runs are derived before any is advanced or whether each run is derived and fully advanced before the next.
open_points.question: What is the exact ordering of recovery writes and externally visible service requests across multiple unfinished runs?
options: Derive all runs first, then fully advance them oldest first
Derive and fully advance each run oldest first
Interleave ready nodes across runs
open_points.default_guess: Derive all runs first, then fully advance runs one at a time in oldest-first order.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision
open_points.text: A08 says the kernel reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` `at the configured manifest_revision`, but no rule defines how a revision is resolved, checked out or read without changing the working tree.
open_points.question: What repository or snapshot mechanism gives `manifest_revision` meaning, and what exact failures occur when the location is not such a repository or the revision is absent?
options: Read files through Git object lookup at the named commit
Require `manifest_location` to already be a revision-specific immutable directory
Ignore the revision and read the working tree
open_points.default_guess: Read the file directly from the named Git commit without checking out or modifying the working tree.

open_points.subject: Manifest JSON duplicate member names
open_points.text: A08 treats an unreadable or invalid-JSON service record as a mismatch and hashes a capability with JCS, but does not say whether JSON objects with duplicate member names are invalid; JCS cannot give an unambiguous meaning to them.
open_points.question: Are duplicate JSON object member names anywhere in a manifest record refused, and at which manifest-mismatch check?
options: Refuse duplicate names during JSON parsing
Keep the first member
Keep the last member
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the record as invalid JSON before reading its fields.

open_points.subject: Service base URLs
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, and A09 forms a request by taking the base URL `without a trailing /` and appending the declared path. It does not address base URLs with a query, fragment, user information, multiple trailing slashes, percent-encoded path segments or an existing path.
open_points.question: Which exact base-URL forms are valid, and precisely how is the operation path joined to a base URL that already contains path or delimiter components?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional normalized path prefix
Allow all absolute URLs and use standards-based URL resolution
Use literal string concatenation after removing exactly one slash
open_points.default_guess: Refuse user information, query and fragment; preserve an existing path prefix and remove all trailing slashes before appending the declared path.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: A09 permits plain HTTP when the `api_base_url` host `is a loopback address`, but does not say whether this means only an IP literal or also a hostname whose DNS resolution currently includes loopback, nor what happens if resolution returns both loopback and non-loopback addresses.
open_points.question: How is the loopback exception determined and prevented from changing through DNS resolution or rebinding?
options: Only loopback IP literals qualify
A hostname qualifies only if every resolved address is loopback
Any hostname currently resolving to loopback qualifies
open_points.default_guess: Only canonical loopback IP literals qualify.

open_points.subject: TLS verification
open_points.text: A09 states only `TLS is verified for https` and does not identify the trust store, hostname-verification rules, client-certificate behavior or handling of custom installation CAs.
open_points.question: What exact trust roots and hostname rules constitute successful TLS verification?
options: Use the pinned runtime's system CA store and standard hostname verification
Use a release-bundled CA set
Allow installation-configured trust roots
open_points.default_guess: Use the host system CA store with standard hostname verification and no client certificate.

open_points.subject: HTTP response classification
open_points.text: A09 classifies 1xx, 2xx, 3xx, 4xx and 5xx outcomes and refers to a `valid final response`, but does not define treatment of out-of-range status codes, conflicting framing headers, unsupported transfer codings, or a response with `Content-Encoding` despite `Accept-Encoding: identity`.
open_points.question: Which HTTP responses count as malformed, and how are unsupported content encodings or nonstandard status codes mapped for read and effectful operations?
options: Treat all such responses as no valid final response
Treat syntactically parseable nonstandard responses by numeric status family and encoded bodies as raw bytes
Delegate validity to the selected HTTP library
open_points.default_guess: Treat unsupported framing or content encoding and status codes outside 200–599 as no valid final response.

open_points.subject: File response Content-Type
open_points.text: A09 compares a file response's `Content-Type` on type and subtype while ignoring parameters, and refuses a missing or doubled header, but does not define behavior for syntactically invalid media types, duplicate parameters or comma-combined values.
open_points.question: What exact media-type parser and validity rules decide whether a file response matches its port?
options: Require one syntactically valid RFC media type and ignore valid parameters
Compare the text before the first semicolon without further validation
Let the HTTP library normalize and choose a value
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one syntactically valid media type and compare its normalized type and subtype.

open_points.subject: Control characters in configuration and manifest headers
open_points.text: A17 rejects a credential containing `a control character`, and A08 rejects required-header values that `hold a control character`, without defining the character set.
open_points.question: Does `control character` mean ASCII C0 plus DEL, C0/C1, or every Unicode character with a control category?
options: ASCII C0 and DEL
Unicode Cc characters
All Unicode control and format characters
open_points.default_guess: Reject ASCII C0 characters and DEL.

open_points.subject: Configuration, secret and manifest input sizes
open_points.text: A20 lists ceilings for surface requests, values, files and service responses, but A16, A17 and A08 give no maximum size for the configuration file, credential file or manifest service record before reading and parsing them.
open_points.question: What bounded size and failure behavior apply to these host and manifest files?
options: Add fixed release ceilings for each file type
Reuse `surface_request_bytes_max`
Leave them unbounded and rely on host operations
open_points.default_guess: Apply explicit release ceilings and refuse startup or the affected service operation when exceeded.

open_points.subject: Constant-time token comparison
open_points.text: A16 requires each token to be compared `in constant time` but permits different token lengths and does not state whether timing must also be independent of token count, match position or early success.
open_points.question: With respect to which properties must authentication timing be constant, and must every configured token be compared on every request?
options: Constant with respect to token contents only
Constant with respect to contents, lengths and match position
Only each equal-length primitive comparison must be constant-time
open_points.default_guess: Compare against every configured token without early exit and make each comparison independent of token contents and length mismatch.

open_points.subject: Data-directory privacy
open_points.text: A18 says the data directory `and everything in it are private to the kernel's user` and that startup refuses otherwise, but unlike A17 it gives no ownership, mode, ACL, hard-link or parent-directory criteria.
open_points.question: What exact filesystem ownership and permission checks define a private data directory and private contents?
options: Kernel ownership and no group/other permission on every entry
Only the top directory must be mode 0700
Use platform ACL checks in addition to Unix mode bits
open_points.default_guess: Require every entry to be owned by the kernel user and to grant no permissions to group or others, while refusing symbolic links.

open_points.subject: Crash durability of store and published files
open_points.text: A18 promises that a crash during a value write leaves either no file or the complete file and that completed named files are never overwritten, but specifies only flushing and renaming; it does not specify database durability, directory fsync, WAL settings or ordering between file publication and transaction commit.
open_points.question: What durability protocol makes database records and their external files consistent after process or host crashes?
options: Fsync temporary files, containing directories and SQLite commits in a defined order
Guarantee only process-crash atomicity, not host-crash durability
Store all payloads inside SQLite transactions
open_points.default_guess: Publish and fsync payload files and directories before committing a fully durable SQLite transaction, accepting only harmless unnamed orphan files.

open_points.subject: Pinned sandbox dependency
open_points.text: A20 says `one release fixes every ceiling and every dependency` and pins Python dependencies and the sandbox runtime, while A03 only checks that `bubblewrap` is present and never fixes a bubblewrap version or compatibility range.
open_points.question: Is bubblewrap part of the release-pinned dependency set, and which versions or capabilities are accepted at startup?
options: Pin one exact bubblewrap version
Probe and accept a declared compatible version range
Treat any version passing the probe as equivalent
open_points.default_guess: Require a declared compatible version range plus capability probes, and include that requirement in the release identity.

open_points.subject: Agent-visible failure-detail length
open_points.text: A07 says a protected `failure_detail` is returned to an agent `only as its length and that class`, but does not say whether length means Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes, original bytes before decoding, or the already truncated stored detail.
open_points.question: Which length is disclosed for a non-open failure detail?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Unicode scalar count of the stored detail
Length of the original untruncated detail
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded detail.

open_points.subject: Configuration re-read validation
open_points.text: A16 says a changed configuration is re-read and `the file can be read and parsed`, that only the token list is taken, and that `Exactly four checks apply to a re-read`; it does not say whether parsing validates the complete installation schema or only syntax and token fields.
open_points.question: Can invalid changes to non-token configuration fields make every request fail during token re-read, or are those fields ignored until restart?
options: Validate only file syntax and token-list shape
Validate the entire installation schema but apply only tokens
Read only a separately encoded token section
open_points.default_guess: Validate syntax and the token-list structure only; ignore all other changed fields until restart.
